Results at a glanceSYS-F catches 54 of 113 adverse labours (sensitivity 0.478, 95% CI 0.388-0.569) at a specificity of 0.793, which is 21 false HIGH RISK alerts per 100 normal labours, warning a median of 15 minutes before the recording ends. Layer 1 alone caught 43. Every number is out-of-fold, with thresholds tuned inside the training folds only. Prototype on retrospective non-Indian data; not for clinical use.

Part 0. How to read this report

Every number here comes from labours the model never saw during training. Thresholds are chosen inside the training folds and applied to the held-out fold, so nothing is tuned on the data it is scored on.

Why not accuracy?Accuracy is not reported as a headline anywhere in this document. With 113 adverse labours among 552, a monitor that called every labour normal would be 79.5% accurate and would catch not one compromised baby. Sensitivity comes first, and the cost of that sensitivity - specificity, false alarms per 100 normal labours, and minutes spent in RED - is printed beside it every time.
Every metric used in this report
termdefinitionreading
SensitivityTP / (TP + FN)share of adverse labours the monitor alarmed on
SpecificityTN / (TN + FP)share of normal labours it left alone
PPVTP / (TP + FP)of the labours it alarmed on, how many were adverse
NPVTN / (TN + FN)of the labours it cleared, how many really were normal
LR+sens / (1 - spec)how much an alarm multiplies the odds of an adverse outcome
LR-(1 - sens) / spechow much silence divides those odds
F2weights recall twice as heavily as precisiona single score that takes missing a baby more seriously
False alarms /100 normal100 x FP / (FP + TN)the workload the alarm creates
NNA1 / PPValerts raised per genuine case found
Lead timefirst HIGH RISK to the end of recordinghow much warning the team gets
Statistical conventionsUnit of analysis is the labour, never the window or the reading. Proportions carry Wilson 95% CIs; AUROC, AUPRC, Brier and net benefit carry percentile CIs from 2,000 bootstrap resamples of labours. Two kinds of threshold appear and are never mixed: the CV-tuned threshold, chosen inside each training fold and applied to its test fold, which is what every headline number uses; and the pooled post-hoc threshold read off the pooled curve, which is optimistic and is labelled illustrative wherever it appears.

1.3 Layer 1 as a whole

1.4 How early does Layer 1 warn?

Reading box: what the rules alone achieveLayer 1 alone catches 43 of 113 adverse labours (sensitivity 0.381, 95% CI 0.296-0.473), missing 70. It does so at a specificity of 0.831, which is 16.9 false alarms per 100 normal labours. When it does warn in an adverse labour, it warns a median of 15 minutes before the recording ends (IQR 6-28). Those 70 missed labours are the entire motivation for Layer 2.

Part 2. Layer 2 alone: the Naive Bayes risk model

Built up in three steps so it is clear where the information comes from: what the history alone says before any trace is seen, what the trace alone says, and what the two say together. The score is the probability at the last reading unless stated otherwise.

2.7 Is the probability believable?

Calibration-in-the-large will not transferCTU-UHB is an enriched sample: 552 labours were selected from 9,164, with caesarean cases deliberately over-represented to balance outcomes. Its 20.5% adverse rate is therefore far above a real ward's. The ranking performance here should transfer; the absolute probabilities should not, and would read too high everywhere. DEPLOY_PREVALENCE in config.py exists for exactly this: it shifts the base log odds to the local rate without refitting a single likelihood ratio.

Reading box: what Layer 2 addsLayer 2 reaches an AUROC of 0.638 on labours it never saw, against 0.588 for the history alone and 0.634 for the trace alone. Published work on CTU-UHB reaches about 0.83 with far more pre-training data, so a figure in this range is a credible result for one day's work and is not something to overclaim. The calibration slope is 0.90, and the net benefit sits above both treat-all and treat-none across the low threshold range where a senior review is worth requesting.

How this operating point was chosenThe operating point is set by an alarm budget, not by a sensitivity target. Theta is the smallest value whose share of alarming labours still fits inside 30%, which is the most sensitive monitor a ward could actually absorb. On the test folds the system alarms on 26.3% of labours and reaches a sensitivity of 0.478 at a specificity of 0.793.

An earlier build targeted 90% sensitivity instead. That rule ran out of grid in every fold, pushed theta to its floor, and produced a monitor that alarmed on about 86% of normal labours - technically sensitive, clinically useless. With a pooled AUROC near 0.64 a monitor simply cannot catch 90% of adverse labours without alarming on most normal ones; the budget rule makes that trade-off explicit instead of hiding it in a degenerate corner. The highest specificity attainable at sensitivity >= 0.90 is 0.216. The table above shows what every other threshold would buy, so the budget can be moved if a ward can absorb more alerts.
Reading box: the system in one paragraphThe combined system catches 54 of 113 adverse labours (sensitivity 0.478, 95% CI 0.388-0.569), missing 59. It does so at a specificity of 0.793, which is 21 false HIGH RISK alerts per 100 normal labours. For the adverse labours it catches it warns a median of 20 minutes before the recording ends. Layer 2 contributes 50 adverse labours that the guideline rules alone never flagged. Compare this with Layer 1 alone, which caught 43 at 17 false alarms per 100.

  • Retrospective, on Czech labour data and Chinese antenatal data. No Indian data. Not validated and not for clinical use.
  • CTU-UHB covers only the last 90 minutes or less before birth, so 'time 0' is the start of the recording, not the true start of monitoring. Abnormal patterns are more common at this point than they would be at a real start.
  • CTU-UHB is a selected sample: 552 labours drawn from 9,164 with caesareans over-represented, so both the prevalence and the performance would differ on an unselected ward.
  • The outcome is a surrogate. Cord acidaemia and a low Apgar are not the same as injury or NICU admission, and the dataset authors report no severe neonatal morbidity in this cohort.
  • Naive Bayes assumes the items are independent given the outcome. Correlated history items and overlapping windows overstate certainty; lambda, gamma and the per-labour window weights reduce this, and the calibration plot measures what remains.
  • The encoder was pre-trained on antenatal traces, so labour-specific patterns such as decelerations with contractions are under-represented in pre-training. There is also no maternal heart-rate channel, so a maternal rate recorded in place of the fetal rate cannot be detected.
  • With only 113 adverse labours, every percentage carries a wide confidence interval. The Layer 1 thresholds still need clinician confirmation.
